pack.problem: AEGIS research trigger: scheduled_cadence. Current PF=None, EV=None
pack.proposed_change: Candidate improvement: a spread-percentile abstention gate, tested shadow-first before any code change. Hypothesis: entries opened when the live spread at signal time falls in the top quartile of its own trailing distribution realize materially lower (possibly negative) mean net-of-cost EV than lower-quartile entries, so abstaining on them raises aggregate expectancy. Method: retrospectively bucket confirmed trades in the existing outcome_log.jsonl by entry-spread percentile, compare net expecta
pack.risks: unvalidated idea; tiny DEMO risk only

concerns: PF/EV are None for scheduled_cadence: there is no baseline evidence the trigger underperforms; the proposed gate addresses entry costs, not signal quality, and may not move aggregate outcomes.

Retrospective bucketing of confirmed trades is selection-biased: trades already survived every gate, and spread percentile will correlate with session/time-of-day/volatility regime, confounding the quartile comparison.
Trailing-distribution percentile is a lookahead hazard: it must be computed strictly from spread observations preceding each entry, with the window documented.
Sample-size risk: quartile splits on a young DEMO outcome log may yield too few trades per bucket for any significant expectancy difference.

expected_mechanism 'improve exploration/validation throughput' contradicts the design: abstention reduces trade count and thus likely reduces validation throughput while raising expectancy. Reconcile.
Falsification criterion references 'exploration trades', implying a live-ordering phase; as written the change is shadow-only, so falsification must be defined on the shadow/retrospective stage.
Data availability unverified: unclear whether entry-spread is reliably recorded in every outcome_log.jsonl row; if not, the retrospective test cannot run without logging-only instrumentation first.
votes.reason: Shadow-first, retrospective-only design on existing outcome_log.jsonl touches neither the execution owner path nor protected trading YAML, so no safety objection. The spread-cost hypothesis is sound microstructure reasoning and the falsification/rollback framing is honest. However the proposal ships with methodological gaps that would invalidate or bias the retrospective test if run as written, plus one internally inconsistent claim (expected_mechanism), so it needs one revision cycle before approval.
requested_revisions: Verify entry-spread field coverage in outcome_log.jsonl first; if incomplete, resubmit with a logging-only instrumentation step (zero behavior change) as phase 1.
Specify the trailing spread-percentile computation precisely: window length, minimum history before first usable percentile, strict no-lookahead guarantee.
Add confounder controls: stratify or regress the quartile comparison by symbol and session/hour, or demonstrate spread percentile is not a proxy for time-of-day.
Define minimum samples per bucket (e.g. >=30) and require a bootstrap confidence interval on the top-vs-lower-quartile net-EV delta excluding zero before any behavior-affecting step is considered.
Correct expected_mechanism to reflect expectancy improvement at the cost of reduced trade count, and restate throughput expectations honestly.
Restate falsification_criteria on the shadow stage: negative costed expectancy delta between top-quartile and remaining buckets, with no DEMO orders placed during the test.

Confirm in writing that any future runtime adoption of the gate routes through the governed promote.py champion pipeline and never edits PROTECTED_LIVE_YAML or non-designated trading configs without operator authorization.

concerns: Trailing distribution window, symbol/session stratification, and percentile calculation are unspecified.
Outcome data must use only information available at entry and remain net of spread, slippage, commissions, and swaps.
Top-quartile comparison can be underpowered or confounded by volatility, time-of-day, liquidity regime, and signal type.
No code or champion promotion should occur until out-of-sample shadow results meet predeclared gates.
votes.reason: Shadow-first research is appropriate, but the proposal lacks a precise, leakage-safe spread-percentile definition, minimum sample requirements, and precommitted decision criteria.
requested_revisions: Define the causal, entry-time-only percentile feature, lookback window, minimum observations, missing-data behavior, and per-symbol/session handling.
Pre-register sample-size thresholds, net-EV/PF metrics, confidence intervals, and an OOS acceptance/falsification rule versus the existing baseline.
Record the experiment in ExperimentRegistry and preserve all buckets, including null/failed results.
Keep the initial implementation research-only/shadow-only; require governed promotion gates before any execution-path or champion change.

concerns: Current PF and EV are unavailable.
The proposal does not specify minimum sample sizes or statistical confidence thresholds.
Entry-spread percentile calculation and cost assumptions need precise definition.
All results must be recorded in ExperimentRegistry and validated out of sample.
votes.reason: The proposal is explicitly shadow-first and retrospective, with no champion, broker, or live-config impact. It is suitable for controlled validation before any implementation.
requested_revisions: Define minimum trade counts per percentile bucket and required confidence or effect-size thresholds.
Specify the trailing-window percentile calculation, timestamp alignment, and missing-data handling.
Report net-of-spread, slippage, and other runner costs consistently, with an untouched OOS holdout.
Confirm the experiment cannot call mt5.order_send(), alter trading YAML, or affect champion promotion.
Register the experiment and record null, negative, or failed results honestly.
